model.name: Review / Inspection / Audit
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to commission, plan, execute, evidence, conclude, report and govern a bounded review, inspection, audit or assessment engagement: who is mandated to examine what, against which criteria, by which methods, on what evidence, yielding which findings, conclusion, assurance level, redress path and record governance.
model.scope_statement: The model is rooted on one engagement occurrence (audit, inspection, review, assessment or attestation engagement) treated as an aggregate: engagement identity governs its plan, execution log, observations, evidence appraisals, findings, conclusion, issued report or certificate, recommendations, appeals and record provenance, which share the engagement lifecycle. It is storage- and interface-neutral; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections, not semantics. It carries references to the examined subject, the criteria sources, the responsible party and any remediation actions, but never reproduces those models' lifecycles. 'Audit' here means an assurance or examination activity, not IT audit-trail logging, which is a homonym.
in_scope: Engagement identity, registration and typing (audit, inspection, review, assessment, attestation, direct-reporting, surveillance, follow-up)
Mandate, statutory or contractual authority, terms of engagement, and appointment of the three parties
Impartiality, independence and conflict-of-interest declarations scoped to this engagement
Subject matter, subject-matter information, scope boundary, period covered and declared exclusions
Selection and binding of criteria to authoritative external requirement sources
Materiality, tolerance, acceptance limits and documented decision rules including measurement-uncertainty handling
Engagement plan, objectives, schedule, methods, sampling strategy, depth and coverage
Fieldwork execution log, site and access conditions, and deviations from plan
Observations, evidence items, custody and integrity, and appraisal of relevance, reliability and sufficiency
Findings with criteria/condition/cause/effect structure, conformity determination and severity grading
Finding identity, recurrence and baseline comparison across engagements
Engagement conclusion, opinion, assurance level and report or certificate issuance with use restrictions
Responsible-party views, right to be heard, appeals and complaints about this engagement
Recommendation issuance and follow-up verification of claimed remediation
Engagement record provenance, versioning, amendment, retention classification and quality review
out_of_scope: The examined subject itself (product, asset, system, process, person, programme) and its own lifecycle
Requirement, regulation and control-catalogue texts; only references, selections and engagement-local interpretations are held here
Corrective and preventive action execution, remediation project management and action closure
Enterprise risk register ownership, risk treatment decisions and residual-risk acceptance
Enforcement measures, sanctions, withdrawal, recall, prosecution and administrative penalties
Certification, approval and accreditation decision lifecycles, including suspension and withdrawal of certificates held by the subject or the body
Laboratory test method definition, measurement execution and uncertainty computation
Auditor qualification, training, certification and competence-registry lifecycle
IT system audit trails, security event logs and continuous telemetry pipelines (homonym boundary)
The multi-engagement audit programme or annual assurance plan and its own prioritisation lifecycle
Runtime policy evaluation, access-control enforcement and the platform audit trail that records who read these records
Physical execution of records disposal, destruction certificates and archival transfer
Commercial terms, fee arrangements and invoicing

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records which criteria were selected, their version binding and any engagement-local interpretation; the catalogue model owns requirement text, hierarchy and its own version lifecycle. OSCAL keeps controls in the catalogue and profile layers and only references them from assessment results.

This model issues recommendations and records follow-up verification observations. Deciding, planning, executing and closing corrective action belongs elsewhere: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 places corrective action on the economic operator and enforcement on the authority, while the market-surveillance authority verifies follow-up.

OSCAL lets an assessment result carry engagement-scoped risk characterizations, but risk-treatment decisions and residual-risk acceptance migrate to the POA&M or risk model. This model therefore carries risk statements produced by the engagement, not the risk register lifecycle.

Measurement values, method validation and uncertainty evaluation are produced by testing or laboratory models. This model consumes them as evidence and applies a documented decision rule, in the JCGM 106 sense, to reach a conformity determination.

Inspection certificates and attestations issued as engagement outputs are in scope as artifacts, but the decision lifecycle of a certification or of a body's accreditation scope is owned by the certification and accreditation models, per the EU accreditation framework.

Article 16 measures, Article 19 serious-risk withdrawal or recall, and any penalty are enforcement acts owned by an enforcement model. This model supplies the evidenced non-compliance determination that such measures may cite.

boundary_notes.neighbor: IT audit-trail and security logging model
boundary_notes.distinction: Homonym boundary. System audit logs are potential evidence sources referenced by observations; this model never owns log-record semantics, log retention or log integrity enforcement.

This model records appointment to an engagement role and the engagement-scoped impartiality declaration; qualification, training and competence-registry lifecycle belong to the party model, as separated in the IIA and INTOSAI frameworks.

Programme-level risk-based prioritisation, coverage across many engagements and resourcing span multiple engagements and have their own lifecycle. This model holds only a reference from the engagement to its programme.

PROV-O is an alignment target for expressing engagement-as-Activity, evidence-as-Entity and auditor-as-Agent. This model does not redefine provenance semantics and does not own generic provenance reasoning.

sources.title: OSCAL Assessment Results Model v1.1.2 JSON Format Metaschema Reference
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

sources.title: Assessment Results Model (OSCAL concepts documentation)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Explains what was assessed, how, by whom, findings and risks; observations record evidence, findings link observations to control objectives, reviewed-controls sets scope, attestations record assessor assertions, and root uuid/last-modified must change on every content change.

sources.title: Assessment Plan Model (OSCAL concepts documentation)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Defines planning constructs: reviewed-controls with control and control-objective selections and assessment methods, assessment subjects (locations, components, inventory items, users), assessment assets (teams, tools), tasks and activities, and terms-and-conditions / rules of engagement.

sources.relevance: Machine-readable finding interchange: run, tool/driver, reportingDescriptor (rule id), result (ruleId, level, kind pass/fail/review/open/informational/notApplicable, message, locations, provenance, suppressions), artifact hashes, invocation, and fingerprints / partialFingerprints with baselineState for stable finding identity across runs.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, wasDerivedFrom, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime/endedAtTime and qualified-influence patterns; alignment target for engagement provenance and evidence derivation chains.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and compliance of products
sources.version_or_date: OJ L 169, 25.6.2019, consolidated text as accessed 2026-08-29
sources.relevance: Article 3 definitions (market surveillance, authority, non-compliance, risk, serious risk, economic operator); Article 11 risk-based checks, documentary, physical and laboratory checks on representative samples, follow-up of complaints and verification of corrective action; Article 14 powers including unannounced inspections and sampling; Article 16 proportionate measures stating exact grounds; Article 18 right to be heard; Article 19 serious risk; Article 21 accredited Union testing facilities; Articles 22-23 mutual assistance; Article 34 information and communication system.

sources.title: ISSAI 100 – Fundamental Principles of Public-Sector Auditing

sources.title: Global Internal Audit Standards
sources.relevance: Five domains and fifteen principles including Demonstrate Integrity, Maintain Objectivity, Demonstrate Competency and Exercise Due Professional Care; Domain V standards for planning engagements effectively, conducting engagement work, and communicating engagement results and monitoring action plans.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Methodology and procedures for control assessment within a risk-management framework; tailorable assessment procedures, assessment plan construction and analysis of assessment results across lifecycle phases.

sources.relevance: Metamodel for structured assurance cases defined as auditable claims, arguments and evidence supporting a claim that a system or service satisfies particular requirements; alignment target for linking criteria-derived claims to evidence and reasoning in a conclusion.

sources.title: JCGM publications, including JCGM 106:2012 'Evaluation of measurement data — The role of measurement uncertainty in conformity assessment' and JCGM 200:2012 (VIM)

sources.title: Commission Notice — The 'Blue Guide' on the implementation of EU product rules 2022
sources.relevance: Explains conformity assessment modules, conformity assessment bodies and notified bodies, accreditation under Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 as the means of demonstrating competence, the role of inspection-body standards, technical documentation, and market-surveillance checks across the product lifecycle.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 17020:2012 Conformity Assessment — Requirements for the Operation of Various Types of Bodies Performing Inspection (OSAC Registry entry)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Organization of Scientific Area Committees for Forensic Science
sources.version_or_date: Registry entry added 7 June 2022; refers to ISO/IEC 17020:2012

sources.title: GAO Issues 2024 'Yellow Book,' Updating the Standards for Government Auditing
sources.relevance: Confirms the 2024 revision's move from quality control to a risk-based system of quality management, the option of engagement quality reviews for GAGAS audits, and application guidance on key audit matters.

bundles.name: Engagement identity and mandate
bundles.description: Establishes what this engagement is, how it is classified, under what authority it is performed, and who occupies which role with what impartiality safeguards.
bundles.rationale: Every verified standard opens the engagement with an identified commission and a party structure: INTOSAI names the three parties, the IIA requires objectivity and competency, GAGAS defines engagement types with distinct requirements, and EU market surveillance derives inspection power from a designated authority. Without a stable identity and an authority basis, no downstream finding is attributable or contestable.

layers.name: Identity and typing
layers.description: Stable identification of the engagement occurrence and the classification that selects which requirement regime, assurance level and reporting form apply.

findings.name: Engagement identifier and registration
findings.description: How a single engagement occurrence is uniquely identified, by which issuing system, and how that identity survives re-issue, merger, split and cross-organisation exchange.

questions.text: Which system of record issues the engagement identifier, and what is its issuing authority and scope of uniqueness?
When no master-system or governed global identifier exists, which surrogate is minted and by whom?
answer_data: Reason no authoritative identifier was available

questions.text: How is identity preserved when an engagement is split, merged, re-opened or superseded by a re-inspection?
Which additional external references identify this engagement to counterparties and authorities?

data_elements.name: engagement_identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the engagement occurrence, qualified by its issuing system and scheme.

data_elements.name: alternate_identifiers
data_elements.description: Set of additional identifiers assigned by counterparties, regulators or exchange systems, each with issuer and scheme.

data_elements.name: engagement_relations
data_elements.description: Typed references to predecessor, successor, parent-programme or parallel engagements.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data carried on the engagement record itself. Materialising it as a separate artifact would create a second identity surface that could drift from the system of record, and no verified standard requires a standalone identity document.

findings.name: Engagement type and assurance classification
findings.description: Classification of the engagement along the dimensions that change its normative obligations: discipline, engagement form, assurance level and reporting model.

questions.text: Which engagement type applies, and which requirement standard governs that type?
answer_data: Engagement type code (financial audit, attestation engagement, review of financial statements, performance audit, compliance audit, management-system audit, product inspection, control assessment, peer review)

questions.text: Is the engagement an attestation or a direct-reporting engagement, and what level of assurance is intended?
answer_data: Assurance level code (reasonable, limited, none/agreed-upon procedures)

questions.text: What triggered this engagement, and is it routine, risk-based, complaint-driven, follow-up or unannounced?
Is the examining body internal, first-party, second-party or third-party relative to the subject?

data_elements.name: engagement_type_code
data_elements.description: Coded engagement type drawn from the governing requirement standard's taxonomy.

data_elements.name: assurance_level_code
data_elements.description: Intended level of assurance, distinguishing reasonable, limited and non-assurance procedures.

data_elements.name: engagement_trigger
data_elements.description: Reason the engagement was initiated, including risk-based selection, complaint, mandate cycle or prior finding.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification consists of coded values and their justification text bound to the engagement record. The code lists themselves are owned by the governing standard's catalogue model, so this finding holds only bindings and rationale, not a document.

layers.name: Mandate, authority and parties
layers.description: The legal, regulatory or contractual basis for examining the subject, the terms agreed, and the appointment and impartiality of the people and bodies involved.

findings.name: Mandate, authority and terms of engagement
findings.description: The instrument that authorises the examination, the powers it confers, its limits, and the agreed terms and conditions or rules of engagement.

questions.text: On what legal, regulatory or contractual basis is this engagement authorised, and which instrument evidences it?
answer_data: Authority basis code (statute, designation, contract, charter, accreditation scope)

questions.text: Which specific powers are conferred, such as entry to premises, unannounced inspection, sampling, document demand or acquisition under cover of identity?
answer_data: Conditions and limits on each power
Jurisdiction in which the power is valid

questions.text: What terms and conditions, rules of engagement, liability limits and safety constraints govern the work?
What does this mandate explicitly not authorise, and where does it hand over to an enforcement or certification decision?
answer_data: Reference to the owning enforcement or certification model

data_elements.name: authority_basis
data_elements.description: Coded basis of authority with a reference to the authorising instrument and its issuing party.

data_elements.name: conferred_powers
data_elements.description: Enumerated powers available for this engagement, each with conditions, limits and jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: rules_of_engagement
data_elements.description: Agreed terms, constraints, prohibitions and preconditions governing how the engagement may be performed.

artifacts.name: Engagement authorization instrument
artifacts.description: The signed or issued instrument that commissions the engagement: engagement letter, work order, statutory inspection notice, designation decision or internal audit charter extract.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing system's instrument reference plus version; bound to the engagement identifier and to the issuing party reference.

findings.name: Party appointment and impartiality safeguards
findings.description: Who acts as auditor or inspector, responsible party and intended user; how roles are appointed; and what impartiality, independence and conflict-of-interest safeguards apply to this engagement.

questions.text: Which parties occupy the auditor, responsible-party and intended-user roles for this engagement?
Which individuals are assigned to the engagement team, in which engagement roles, and for which periods?
What threats to impartiality or independence were identified, and which safeguards were applied?
Who declared absence or presence of conflicts of interest, when, and to whom was it disclosed?

data_elements.name: engagement_party_roles
data_elements.description: Assignment of parties and individuals to engagement roles with validity periods.

data_elements.name: impartiality_assessment
data_elements.description: Recorded threats to impartiality or independence, safeguards applied and the residual conclusion.

artifacts.name: Impartiality and conflict-of-interest declaration
artifacts.description: Per-individual or per-body declaration covering independence, conflicts of interest and confidentiality undertakings for this engagement, with the approval of any residual threat.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by declaring-party reference plus engagement identifier plus declaration sequence; superseded rather than overwritten when circumstances change.

bundles.name: Subject matter, criteria and decision basis
bundles.description: Fixes what is examined, the boundary and period of examination, the criteria the subject is measured against, and the documented rules by which measured or observed states become conformity determinations.
bundles.rationale: INTOSAI states subject matter, criteria and subject-matter information as core elements of any audit, and OSCAL scopes an assessment by reviewed controls and control objectives. JCGM 106 shows that turning a measurement into a conformity statement requires a documented decision rule and explicit treatment of uncertainty; EU market surveillance requires proportionate measures stating exact grounds, which presupposes stated criteria.

layers.name: Subject matter and scope
layers.description: What is being examined, in what representation, within which boundary, over which period, and with what declared exclusions.

findings.name: Subject matter and subject-matter information
findings.description: Distinguishes the underlying subject matter from the subject-matter information presented about it, and identifies the concrete assessment subjects examined.

questions.text: What is the underlying subject matter, and what subject-matter information about it is being examined?
answer_data: Subject-matter information reference (statement, report, dataset, declaration)

questions.text: Which concrete assessment subjects fall within the examination, such as locations, components, inventory items, users, batches or processes?
How does each assessment subject link to the master record for that entity in its owning model?
What was the state or configuration of the subject at the moment of examination, and how was that state captured?

data_elements.name: subject_matter
data_elements.description: Description of the underlying subject matter and, where applicable, a reference to the subject-matter information asserted about it.

data_elements.name: assessment_subjects
data_elements.description: References to concrete subjects included in the examination, with type, selection basis and link to the owning master record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject matter is expressed as typed references into models that own the examined entities, plus a short descriptive statement. Creating a local artifact would duplicate records that the asset, product or system models already govern and would risk divergence from their master state.

findings.name: Scope boundary, period and exclusions
findings.description: The declared limits of the examination in organisational, geographic, temporal and topical terms, including what was deliberately excluded and why.

questions.text: What organisational, contractual and topical boundary is claimed for this engagement?
answer_data: Processes, product families or control families in scope

questions.text: Which period does the examination cover, and how does it relate to the fieldwork dates?
answer_data: As-at date for point-in-time subject matter

questions.text: Which physical or logical locations, sites, borders or jurisdictions are within the examination boundary?
answer_data: Remote versus on-site designation per location

questions.text: What was excluded from scope, on whose decision, and what effect does the exclusion have on the conclusion?

data_elements.name: scope_boundary
data_elements.description: Structured statement of organisational, topical, geographic and jurisdictional limits of the examination.

data_elements.name: period_covered
data_elements.description: Interval of subject-matter activity covered by the engagement, distinct from the fieldwork interval.

data_elements.name: scope_exclusions
data_elements.description: Declared exclusions with deciding party, justification and assessed effect on the conclusion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Boundary, period and exclusions are structured attributes of the engagement that must remain queryable and comparable across engagements. They are rendered inside the plan and report artifacts, but the authoritative values are inline fields rather than a separate document.

layers.name: Criteria and decision basis
layers.description: The requirements the subject is measured against and the documented rules that convert observed or measured states into conformity determinations.

findings.name: Criteria selection and authoritative binding
findings.description: Which criteria apply, from which authoritative source and version, how they were selected or tailored, and how each is interpreted for this engagement.

questions.text: Which authoritative source and version supplies each criterion, and how is that binding resolved at read time?
How were criteria selected, tailored or narrowed to control objectives for this engagement, and who approved the selection?
answer_data: Selection method (full set, profile, risk-based subset)

questions.text: Are the criteria suitable, relevant, complete, reliable, neutral and understandable for the intended users?
answer_data: Justification where criteria are established by the auditor rather than by an authority

questions.text: What engagement-local interpretation or acceptance guidance is applied to an ambiguous criterion, and does it conflict with the source?

data_elements.name: criteria_bindings
data_elements.description: Per-criterion binding to an external source identifier and version, with resolution method and any engagement-local interpretation.

data_elements.name: criteria_suitability_assessment
data_elements.description: Assessment of the criteria against relevance, completeness, reliability, neutrality and understandability for the intended users.

artifacts.name: Engagement criteria register
artifacts.description: The resolved set of criteria and control objectives in scope for this engagement, each bound to its authoritative source and version, with tailoring decisions and local interpretations. It holds bindings only; the criteria text remains owned by the catalogue model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus register version; each entry keyed by the external criterion identifier and its source version.

findings.name: Materiality, tolerance and decision rules
findings.description: The thresholds and documented decision rules that determine when a deviation is reportable and when a measured value counts as conforming, including guard bands and uncertainty treatment.

questions.text: What materiality or significance thresholds apply, quantitatively and qualitatively, and how were they set?
What documented decision rule converts a measured value plus its uncertainty into a conformity determination?
answer_data: Permitted probability of false accept or false reject

questions.text: How is measurement uncertainty obtained and whose responsibility is it to evaluate it?
answer_data: Reference to the owning test or measurement model

questions.text: How does the risk-based prioritisation of checks influence thresholds, sample intensity and reporting?

data_elements.name: materiality_thresholds
data_elements.description: Quantitative and qualitative thresholds determining reportability, with basis and approver.

data_elements.name: decision_rule
data_elements.description: Documented rule mapping measured value and uncertainty onto conformity, including tolerance limits, acceptance limits and guard band.

data_elements.name: risk_prioritisation_basis
data_elements.description: Recorded risk factors and method used to prioritise checks, coverage and thresholds for this engagement.

artifacts.name: Decision rule and materiality statement
artifacts.description: The agreed, dated statement of decision rules, tolerance and acceptance limits, guard bands and materiality thresholds applied in this engagement, referenced by every conformity determination made.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus statement version; where a scheme-wide rule applies, carries a reference to the governing scheme rule identifier and version.

bundles.name: Planning and fieldwork
bundles.description: Converts the mandate and criteria into an executable plan with methods, sampling and coverage, and records what was actually done, where, when and by whom, including departures from plan.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL's assessment plan makes objectives, methods, subjects, assets, tasks and rules of engagement explicit and separates them from results; the IIA requires effective engagement planning and conduct; EU market surveillance requires checks on an adequate scale using documentary, physical and laboratory means on representative samples. The execution record is what makes a conclusion reproducible and contestable.

layers.name: Engagement planning
layers.description: Objectives, schedule, methods, sampling, depth and coverage, and the assets and tooling used to perform the work.

findings.name: Engagement objectives, plan and schedule
findings.description: The stated objectives of the engagement, the tasks and milestones planned to meet them, and the resources committed.

questions.text: What are the engagement objectives, and how does each trace to a criterion or control objective?
answer_data: Traceability links to criteria or control objectives

questions.text: What tasks, activities and milestones are planned, in what sequence, and with which dependencies?
Who approved the plan, when, and what changes require re-approval?
What communication with the responsible party is planned before, during and after fieldwork?

data_elements.name: engagement_objectives
data_elements.description: Stated objectives with traceability to criteria or control objectives and assigned priority.

data_elements.name: planned_tasks
data_elements.description: Planned tasks, activities, milestones, dependencies and responsible roles with planned timings.

artifacts.name: Engagement plan
artifacts.description: The approved plan covering objectives, scope, schedule, team, communication and terms of engagement, versioned and re-approved when materially changed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus plan version; each version records its approver and approval timestamp and supersedes rather than replaces the prior version.

findings.name: Methods, sampling, depth and coverage
findings.description: Which examination methods are applied to which subjects, how samples are drawn from populations, and what depth and coverage are claimed.

questions.text: Which examination methods are used per objective, such as document examination, interview, observation, test, physical check or laboratory analysis?
answer_data: Objects the method is applied to (specifications, mechanisms, activities, individuals)

questions.text: How is the sample drawn from the population, and is the approach judgement-based or statistical?
What depth and coverage are claimed, and what does that imply about the extrapolation of results to the population?
Which tools, platforms and automated analysers are used, at which versions and configurations?

data_elements.name: method_assignments
data_elements.description: Mapping of examination methods to objectives, subjects and object classes, with procedure references.

data_elements.name: sampling_plan
data_elements.description: Population definition, sample size, selection method and representativeness justification.

data_elements.name: assessment_assets
data_elements.description: Tools, analysers and platforms used, with version, rule-set version and configuration.

artifacts.name: Method and sampling protocol
artifacts.description: The documented examination procedures, work programme, sampling scheme and tool configuration applied, sufficient for an independent party to repeat the procedure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus protocol version; references any standing scheme procedure by its own identifier and version rather than copying it.

layers.name: Fieldwork execution
layers.description: The record of what was actually performed, under what conditions and access, by whom, and how execution departed from plan.

findings.name: Fieldwork execution log, conditions and deviations
findings.description: Chronological record of performed actions with actor, time and location, the site and access conditions that constrained them, and any departures from the approved plan.

questions.text: Which assessment actions were performed, by whom, and at what start and end times?
Where was each action performed, and was it on-site, remote or at a border or testing facility?
answer_data: Location mode code (on-site, remote, border, laboratory)

questions.text: What access, availability, safety or security conditions constrained execution?
Where did execution deviate from the approved plan, why, who authorised it, and what is the consequence for coverage?
answer_data: Assessed effect on coverage and conclusion

data_elements.name: assessment_log_entries
data_elements.description: Serial entries recording performed actions with actor, timing, location and related planned task.

data_elements.name: execution_conditions
data_elements.description: Access, availability, safety and security conditions encountered, with their effect on the action.

data_elements.name: plan_deviations
data_elements.description: Recorded departures from the approved plan with reason, authorisation and assessed effect on coverage.

artifacts.name: Fieldwork execution log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of assessment actions performed during the engagement, each with actor, timestamps, location mode, conditions and any deviation from plan.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each entry identified by engagement identifier plus a monotonically increasing entry sequence and the entry's own surrogate identifier; entries are never edited, only superseded by a correcting entry that references the original.

bundles.name: Evidence and observation
bundles.description: How raw observations are captured with their collection method and subject, how evidence items are identified, held and kept intact, and how their relevance, reliability and sufficiency are appraised.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL models observations separately from findings, with methods, subjects, origins, relevant evidence and collection and expiry times, and SARIF attaches artifact hashes and provenance to results. INTOSAI requires sufficient and appropriate evidence; EU market surveillance permits evidence gathered by one authority to support another's investigation, which only works if integrity and appraisal are recorded.

layers.name: Evidence acquisition
layers.description: Capture of observations and the identification, custody and integrity of the evidence items that support them.

findings.name: Observation record and collection method
findings.description: An atomic recorded observation: what was seen or measured, by which method, about which subject, when collected and when it ceases to be current.

questions.text: What exactly was observed, expressed independently of any judgement about conformity?
By which collection method was the observation obtained, and by which actor or tool?
answer_data: Collection method code (examine, interview, test, observe, automated analysis)

questions.text: When was the observation collected, when did the observed condition occur, and when does the observation expire?
answer_data: Ingestion timestamp into the record system

questions.text: Which evidence items support this observation, and are they sufficient on their own?

data_elements.name: observation
data_elements.description: Atomic observation with type, subject, description and origin, recorded without a conformity judgement.

data_elements.name: observation_methods
data_elements.description: Collection methods applied to produce the observation, with the actor or tool origin.

data_elements.name: observation_time_set
data_elements.description: Separate collected, occurred, ingested and expiry timestamps for the observation.

artifacts.name: Observation record
artifacts.description: A single recorded observation with its methods, subjects, origins, timing and links to supporting evidence, usable both to demonstrate conformity and to underpin a nonconformity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a surrogate identifier assigned at capture, scoped by the engagement identifier; carries the origin actor or tool reference and is immutable after the engagement is issued.

findings.name: Evidence item identity, custody and integrity
findings.description: Identification of each evidence item, where it came from, who held it, and how its integrity is demonstrable to a challenging party.

questions.text: How is each evidence item identified, and what is its authoritative source location?
What integrity mechanism demonstrates that the item has not changed since acquisition?
Who has held the item since acquisition, in which transfers, and under what storage conditions?
answer_data: Custody transfer entries with holder, timestamp and reason

questions.text: Does the item contain personal, commercially confidential or classified material, and what handling class applies?
Under what conditions may the item be reused or shared with another authority or engagement?

data_elements.name: evidence_item
data_elements.description: An identified item of evidence with source, type, acquisition method and format.

data_elements.name: evidence_integrity_digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest with algorithm identifier and verification record demonstrating item integrity.

data_elements.name: custody_chain
data_elements.description: Ordered custody transfers with holder, timestamp, reason and storage conditions.

data_elements.name: evidence_sensitivity
data_elements.description: Sensitivity classification, personal-data categories and handling constraints for the item.

artifacts.name: Evidence item package
artifacts.description: The retained or referenced evidence itself: documents, samples, photographs, extracts, test reports, screenshots or tool output, held with format, digest and sensitivity classification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the source system's item identifier where one exists, otherwise a surrogate assigned at acquisition; always paired with a digest and an acquisition timestamp.

artifacts.name: Chain-of-custody record
artifacts.description: Ordered record of possession and transfer of an evidence item from acquisition to disposition, enabling a challenging party to test integrity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by evidence item identifier plus transfer sequence; append-only, with corrections recorded as new entries referencing the original.

layers.name: Evidence appraisal
layers.description: Judgement about whether the evidence obtained is relevant, reliable, sufficient and appropriate, and what limitations qualify it.

findings.name: Relevance, reliability, sufficiency and limitations
findings.description: The recorded appraisal of evidence quality against the objectives, together with scope restrictions, unavailable evidence and their effect on the conclusion.

questions.text: Is each item of evidence relevant to the objective and criterion it is used to support?
How reliable is the evidence given its source, generation method and susceptibility to manipulation?
Is the accumulated evidence sufficient and appropriate to support the intended level of assurance?
What evidence could not be obtained, why, and how does that limit the finding or conclusion?
answer_data: Cause code (access refused, destroyed, out of period, not retained)
Modification to the opinion where applicable

data_elements.name: evidence_appraisal
data_elements.description: Per-item or per-link appraisal of relevance and reliability with justification and assessor.

data_elements.name: sufficiency_conclusion
data_elements.description: Judgement that accumulated evidence is or is not sufficient and appropriate for the intended assurance level.

data_elements.name: evidence_limitations
data_elements.description: Scope restrictions and unavailable evidence, with cause and assessed effect on the conclusion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Appraisal is professional judgement expressed as structured attributes attached to evidence items, observations and evidence-to-criterion links. Emitting it as a standalone artifact would detach the judgement from the item it qualifies and invite inconsistency between the two; the working-paper rendering is a projection of these inline fields.

bundles.name: Findings, conclusion and reporting
bundles.description: How evidence becomes a structured finding with a conformity determination and severity, how findings retain identity across engagements, and how the engagement reaches and communicates a conclusion.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL distinguishes observations from findings that carry control-objective status; SARIF gives results a rule reference, level, kind and stable fingerprints with baseline state; GAGAS and INTOSAI require findings developed against criteria and reported with the views of responsible officials. Reporting is where use restrictions and confidentiality obligations attach.

layers.name: Finding construction
layers.description: The internal structure of a finding, the determination and grading applied to it, and how it is identified and matched over time.

findings.name: Finding statement structure
findings.description: The elements that make a finding intelligible and contestable: the criterion, the condition observed, the cause and the actual or potential effect, with traceability to observations.

questions.text: For this finding, what are the criterion, the observed condition, the cause and the effect or potential effect?
Which observations and evidence items support each element of the finding?
What reasoning connects the evidence to the claim that the criterion is or is not met?
Are the grounds stated precisely enough to support a proportionate measure or a contested response?

data_elements.name: finding_elements
data_elements.description: Criterion reference, condition, cause and effect statements forming the body of the finding.

data_elements.name: finding_traceability
data_elements.description: Links from the finding to the observations, evidence items and criteria that support it.

artifacts.name: Finding record
artifacts.description: A single structured finding carrying its criterion binding, condition, cause, effect, determination, severity, supporting observations and any responsible-party response.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a surrogate identifier assigned on creation, scoped by the engagement identifier, plus a recurrence key computed from criterion, subject and condition signature for cross-engagement matching.

findings.name: Conformity determination and severity grading
findings.description: The verdict attached to a finding against its criterion and the severity or significance grade assigned, with the scheme that defines the permitted values.

questions.text: What determination is recorded against the criterion, and from which controlled value set?
answer_data: Determination value (for example satisfied, other than satisfied, conforming, non-conforming, not applicable, not tested)

questions.text: What severity, significance or risk grade is assigned, under which grading scheme?
Which decision rule and uncertainty treatment produced the determination for a measured characteristic?
On what basis is a criterion recorded as not applicable, not tested or inconclusive rather than passed or failed?

data_elements.name: conformity_determination
data_elements.description: Coded verdict against a criterion, bound to a versioned value set and attributed to a determining party.

data_elements.name: severity_grade
data_elements.description: Severity, significance or risk grade with the identifier and version of the grading scheme used.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The determination and grade are typed attributes of a finding record that already exists as an artifact. Duplicating them into a separate artifact would create two authoritative verdicts for one finding; the grading scheme itself is owned by the criteria or scheme model and is referenced here by identifier and version.

findings.name: Finding identity, recurrence and baseline comparison
findings.description: How a finding keeps a stable identity across engagements and report revisions so that new, unchanged, updated and closed findings can be distinguished and trends measured.

questions.text: What stable key identifies the same underlying issue across engagements even when the artifact or wording changes?
Against which baseline engagement is this finding compared, and what is its baseline state?
answer_data: Baseline state code (new, unchanged, updated, absent)

questions.text: Is this a repeat finding, and how many consecutive engagements has it persisted through?
Has the finding been suppressed, accepted or excluded from reporting, on whose authority and with what justification?

data_elements.name: recurrence_key
data_elements.description: Stable computed key enabling matching of the same underlying issue across engagements and revisions.

data_elements.name: baseline_state
data_elements.description: Comparison state of the finding relative to a nominated baseline engagement.

data_elements.name: suppression_record
data_elements.description: Suppression or reporting-exclusion decision with justification, authorising party and validity period.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Recurrence keys, baseline states and suppression decisions are computed or decided attributes carried on the finding record and on the engagement-to-engagement comparison. They have no independent document existence, and materialising them separately would let the derived state diverge from the finding it describes.

layers.name: Conclusion and reporting
layers.description: Aggregation of findings into an engagement-level conclusion at a stated assurance level, and the issuance of the report or certificate with responsible-party views and use restrictions.

findings.name: Engagement conclusion and assurance statement
findings.description: How individual findings aggregate into an overall conclusion or opinion, at what assurance level, with what modifications and emphases.

questions.text: What is the overall conclusion or opinion, and how does it follow from the findings and their severity?
What level of assurance is expressed, and does it match the level planned?
Is the conclusion modified, qualified, adverse or a disclaimer, and on what grounds?
Which assertions does the examining party itself attest to, and who signs them?

data_elements.name: engagement_conclusion
data_elements.description: Overall conclusion or opinion with its type, aggregation rule and driving findings.

data_elements.name: conclusion_modification
data_elements.description: Modification, qualification, adverse conclusion or disclaimer with its grounds and affected scope.

data_elements.name: attestation_statements
data_elements.description: Assertions made by the examining party, with signing party and signature timestamp.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The conclusion is a structured statement carried on the engagement record so that it remains machine-comparable and independent of any rendering. It is presented inside the report artifact, but treating the rendered text as authoritative would make the conclusion format-dependent and would break comparison across engagements.

findings.name: Report issuance, responsible-party views and use restrictions
findings.description: Issuance of the engagement report or certificate, incorporation of the responsible party's views, and the restrictions on distribution, reliance and publication attached to it.

questions.text: Who issues the report or certificate, to which addressees, and on what date does it take effect?
How were the responsible party's views obtained and represented, including any disagreement?
What restrictions govern reliance, onward distribution, publication and use of the report or certificate?
Which mandatory content and statements must the report carry under the governing standard or law?
answer_data: Grounds statement where a measure may follow

data_elements.name: issuance_record
data_elements.description: Issuing party, addressees, issue timestamp and effective or expiry dates of the report or certificate.

data_elements.name: responsible_party_views
data_elements.description: Views, comments or disagreement of the responsible party, with request and response timestamps.

data_elements.name: use_restrictions
data_elements.description: Reliance, distribution, publication and confidentiality restrictions attached to the issued output.

artifacts.name: Engagement report
artifacts.description: The issued report communicating scope, criteria, work performed, findings, conclusion, responsible-party views and restrictions on use, in whatever rendering the recipient requires.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus report version; each issued version is sealed with a digest, records its issue timestamp and issuing party, and supersedes rather than replaces earlier versions.

artifacts.name: Inspection certificate or attestation
artifacts.description: A short-form issued statement of the examination outcome for a specific item, batch, installation or system, typically with validity dates and defined reliance conditions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing body's certificate number where one exists, otherwise a surrogate, always bound to the engagement identifier and to the examined subject reference. The certification decision lifecycle remains with the certification model.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, record governance and exchange
bundles.description: The engagement state machine and closure, redress and follow-up, the provenance, retention and quality governance of the engagement record set, and its exchange with other systems and standards.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL requires the root identifier and last-modified value to change on every content change, PROV-O supplies the vocabulary for attributing that change, EU market surveillance grants a right to be heard and requires follow-up of complaints and verification of corrective action, and GAGAS 2024 introduces a risk-based system of quality management with optional engagement quality reviews. Exchange with SARIF, OSCAL and PROV is what makes findings comparable beyond the issuing organisation.

layers.name: Engagement lifecycle and redress
layers.description: States the engagement passes through, the recommendations it leaves behind and their verification, and the routes by which its results can be contested.

findings.name: Engagement state model and closure
findings.description: The permitted states of an engagement, the transitions between them, who may effect each transition, and the conditions for closure or abandonment.

questions.text: Which states may an engagement occupy, and which transitions are permitted between them?
answer_data: Entry and exit conditions per state

questions.text: Who is authorised to effect each transition, and what evidence must exist before it is allowed?
What conditions must hold for the engagement to be closed, and what remains open after closure?
How is an engagement suspended, withdrawn or abandoned, and how is partial work disclosed?

data_elements.name: engagement_state
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the engagement drawn from a governed value set.

data_elements.name: state_transitions
data_elements.description: Ordered transition history with actor, timestamp, preconditions satisfied and approval reference.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Lifecycle state and its transition history are governed attributes of the engagement aggregate, expressed as a code plus an append-only transition list. A separate artifact would create a second source of truth for status; the platform workflow engine that drives transitions is referenced, not owned, by this model.

findings.name: Recommendation issuance and follow-up verification
findings.description: Recommendations or required actions arising from findings, and the later verification that claimed remediation is evidenced, without owning the remediation work itself.

questions.text: What recommendation or required action does each finding carry, addressed to whom and by when?
Which model owns the planning, execution and closure of the resulting action, and what is referenced from here?
answer_data: Owning remediation or enforcement model reference

questions.text: How and when is implementation verified, by which procedure, and with what evidence?
What happens when verification fails or the deadline passes, and to whom is it escalated?
answer_data: Reference to the enforcement or governance model that acts

data_elements.name: recommendation
data_elements.description: Recommendation or required action linked to a finding, with addressee and requested completion date.

data_elements.name: remediation_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the action record in the owning remediation, corrective-action or enforcement model.

data_elements.name: followup_verification_outcome
data_elements.description: Outcome of verifying claimed implementation, with method, verifying party, timestamp and evidence links.

artifacts.name: Recommendation record
artifacts.description: A single recommendation or required action arising from a finding, with addressee, requested completion date and a reference to the action record owned by the remediation model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Surrogate identifier scoped by the engagement identifier and bound to the originating finding identifier; carries a reference to, and never a copy of, the action record in the owning remediation model.

artifacts.name: Follow-up verification record
artifacts.description: Record of a verification act confirming or rejecting claimed implementation, with method, evidence and outcome. It records verification only; it does not close the underlying action.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Surrogate identifier scoped by the recommendation identifier plus verification sequence; where verification is performed as a distinct engagement, also carries that engagement's identifier.

findings.name: Right to be heard, appeals and complaints
findings.description: Procedural rights of the responsible party before and after a result is recorded, and the handling of appeals against a determination or complaints about the conduct of the engagement.

questions.text: Was the affected party given the opportunity to be heard before the result was acted on, with what notice period?
Who may appeal which determination, to which body, and within what time limit?
How is the appeal or complaint reviewed independently of the individuals who produced the original result?
What outcomes can an appeal produce, and how are they reflected in the engagement record and any issued output?
answer_data: Outcome code (upheld, partially upheld, rejected, withdrawn)
Amendment or withdrawal of the finding or report

data_elements.name: hearing_record
data_elements.description: Notice, grounds communicated, response window and response for the affected party's right to be heard.

data_elements.name: appeal_case
data_elements.description: Appeal or complaint with appellant, target determination, reviewing body, independence basis and outcome.

artifacts.name: Appeal or complaint case record
artifacts.description: Record of an appeal against a determination or a complaint about the conduct of the engagement, including independence of the reviewer, outcome and any consequent amendment or withdrawal.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the handling body's case reference where one exists, otherwise a surrogate; bound to the engagement identifier and to the specific determination or finding contested.

layers.name: Record governance and quality
layers.description: Provenance and amendment of the engagement record set, its retention classification and disposition, and the quality review that supports reliance on it.

findings.name: Record provenance, versioning and amendment
findings.description: How every change to the engagement record set is attributed, timestamped and versioned, and how an issued output is corrected without rewriting history.

questions.text: Which agent generated or modified each record, acting on behalf of which organisation?
How is a content change signalled, and what identifier and modification timestamp must change with it?
How is an issued report or finding corrected, withdrawn or re-issued, and how is the original preserved?
answer_data: Amendment type code (erratum, correction, withdrawal, re-issue)

questions.text: From which prior records is this record derived, including imported plans and prior engagements?

data_elements.name: record_provenance
data_elements.description: Agent, activity, delegation and timing information attributing generation and modification of each record.

data_elements.name: record_version
data_elements.description: Version identifier and last-modified timestamp that must change whenever record content changes.

data_elements.name: amendment_record
data_elements.description: Amendment, withdrawal or re-issue of a previously issued output, with reason, superseded version and recipient notification.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance and version metadata are properties of every record in the aggregate rather than a document in their own right. Externalising them would decouple attribution from the record it attributes; the platform activity log that records who touched a record is referenced by, and not owned by, this model.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and legal hold
findings.description: Classification of engagement records for retention, the trigger and period that govern disposition, and holds that suspend it, without asserting ownership of disposal execution.

questions.text: Which retention class applies to each record type in this engagement, and which schedule authority defines it?
answer_data: Retention class code per record type

questions.text: What event starts the retention clock, and when does the disposition become due?
Is a legal, regulatory or appeal-related hold in force, who placed it and when may it be released?
Which model or Dimension policy executes disposition, and what tombstone remains here afterwards?
answer_data: Owning records-management model or policy reference

questions.text: How are personal-data minimisation and erasure obligations reconciled with evidentiary retention duties?

data_elements.name: retention_class
data_elements.description: Retention classification per record type with schedule authority, jurisdiction and minimum period.

data_elements.name: retention_trigger
data_elements.description: Event that starts the retention clock and the computed disposition due date.

data_elements.name: legal_hold
data_elements.description: Hold suspending disposition, with placing authority, placement timestamp and release condition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention is expressed as classification and hold attributes plus references to an externally owned retention schedule. This model deliberately holds no disposal artifact because the execution of destruction, transfer and disposal certification belongs to the records-management model and the adopting Dimension's policy, and claiming an artifact here would imply ownership of that execution.

findings.name: Engagement quality review and competence evidence
findings.description: The review performed on the engagement itself before issuance and the evidence that assigned personnel were competent for it, as required by a risk-based system of quality management.

questions.text: Was an engagement quality review performed, by whom, and what was its scope and conclusion?
Under which risk-based criteria is an engagement quality review required rather than optional?
What evidence shows that each assigned individual was competent for their engagement role?
answer_data: Competence evidence references in the owning party model

questions.text: How was the work supervised and reviewed within the engagement team before conclusions were formed?

data_elements.name: engagement_quality_review
data_elements.description: Record of the engagement quality review with reviewer, independence basis, scope, conclusion and timestamp.

data_elements.name: competence_evidence_references
data_elements.description: References into the owning party or competence model demonstrating role fitness for this engagement.

artifacts.name: Engagement quality review record
artifacts.description: The record of the review of the engagement performed before issuance, covering scope, significant judgements examined, matters raised and the reviewer's conclusion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by engagement identifier plus review sequence; bound to the reviewer party reference and to the report version it clears for issue.

layers.name: Exchange and alignment
layers.description: How engagement records are projected onto external exchange standards without asserting conformance, and where those mappings lose information.

findings.name: Exchange binding and standard crosswalk
findings.description: Declared mappings between this model's concepts and external exchange formats and ontologies, with explicit statements of lossiness, direction and version dependence.

questions.text: Which external standard and version is each binding declared against, and in which direction is it valid?
Which local concept maps to which target construct, and which local concepts have no target equivalent?
Where is the mapping lossy or semantically approximate, and what is the effect on a consumer?
What conformance is claimed, and what evidence supports the claim?
answer_data: Conformance claim level (aligned, partially conformant, none claimed)

questions.text: Under what conditions may an engagement record be transmitted to another authority or system, and what must accompany it?

data_elements.name: binding_target
data_elements.description: External standard identifier, version and mapping direction for a declared exchange binding.

data_elements.name: mapping_entries
data_elements.description: Concept-to-construct mapping entries with lossiness annotations and unmapped-concept lists.

data_elements.name: conformance_claim
data_elements.description: Declared conformance level with supporting validation evidence, validating party and timestamp.

artifacts.name: Exchange binding profile
artifacts.description: A versioned, machine-readable crosswalk from this model's concepts to an external target such as OSCAL assessment results, SARIF results or PROV-O, with lossiness annotations and the conformance level actually claimed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by target standard identifier plus target version plus binding version; each binding is independently versioned from the model so a target revision does not force a model revision.

functions.name: Register engagement
functions.description: Create the engagement aggregate root with its identity, classification, mandate reference and party roles, making it addressable before any planning or fieldwork occurs.
inputs: Authority basis and authorising instrument reference
Engagement type and intended assurance level
Party references for auditor, responsible party and intended users
Master-system identifier if issued, otherwise a minted surrogate
outputs: Registered engagement record with resolved identifier
preconditions: An authorising instrument or designation exists and is referenced
The issuing system for the identifier is declared
Engagement type maps to a governing requirement standard
effects: Engagement becomes addressable and referenceable by other records
Identifier and issuing authority are fixed and thereafter immutable
Lifecycle state set to the initial planned or commissioned state

functions.name: Bind criteria set
functions.description: Resolve and attach the criteria and control objectives in scope for the engagement, each bound to an external source identifier and version, with tailoring decisions and local interpretations recorded.
outputs: Traceability links from objectives to criteria
preconditions: Engagement is registered
Criteria sources resolve to a specific version
Selection is approved by an authorised role
effects: Findings can be created only against bound criteria
Criteria versions are pinned for the engagement, insulating it from later catalogue revisions
No criterion text is copied locally; only bindings and interpretations are stored

functions.name: Record observation
functions.description: Capture an atomic observation with its collection method, subject, origin actor or tool, supporting evidence references and separated event, collection and ingestion timestamps.
preconditions: Engagement is in an executing state
Collection method is one declared in the method and sampling protocol
Any evidence item referenced has an integrity digest recorded
effects: Observation becomes available for finding construction
Execution log gains an append-only entry
No conformity judgement is asserted by this operation

functions.name: Appraise evidence
functions.description: Record the judgement of relevance, reliability, sufficiency and appropriateness for evidence supporting an objective, together with limitations and unavailable evidence.
preconditions: Observations and evidence items exist
The targeted assurance level is declared
Assessor is assigned to an engagement role
effects: Sufficiency conclusion becomes a precondition for issuing an engagement conclusion
Limitations propagate to scope and to any conclusion modification
Appraisal is attributed to a named assessor and timestamp

functions.name: Construct finding and determine conformity
functions.description: Assemble criterion, condition, cause and effect into a finding, attach the supporting observations, apply the documented decision rule and record the determination and severity grade.
inputs: Decision rule and materiality statement reference
outputs: Finding record with determination and severity
Traceability links to observations and evidence
preconditions: Criterion is bound with a pinned version
At least one supporting observation exists
A decision rule is referenced where a measured characteristic is involved
effects: Finding becomes citable by recommendations, reports and appeals
Recurrence key enables cross-engagement matching
Grounds are stated precisely enough to support a contested response

functions.name: Issue conclusion and report
functions.description: Aggregate findings into an engagement conclusion at a stated assurance level, incorporate the responsible party's views, and issue the sealed report or certificate with its use restrictions.
outputs: Inspection certificate or attestation where applicable
preconditions: Evidence sufficiency is concluded
Responsible party has been given the opportunity to comment
Any required engagement quality review has been completed
effects: Report version is sealed with a digest and becomes immutable
Findings become append-only; later change requires an amendment or re-issue
Certification and enforcement decisions that may follow remain owned by their models

functions.name: Register appeal or complaint
functions.description: Record a challenge to a determination or to the conduct of the engagement, assign an independent reviewer, and capture the outcome and any consequent amendment.
outputs: Outcome and any amendment or withdrawal reference
preconditions: The contested determination exists and is identified
The appellant is eligible under the declared appeal route
The assigned reviewer is independent of the original engagement team
effects: Disposition of the affected records is suspended while the appeal is open
An upheld appeal triggers an amendment, re-issue or withdrawal
This model records the appeal outcome; it does not conduct legal proceedings or enforcement

functions.name: Record follow-up verification
functions.description: Record a verification act testing whether claimed implementation of a recommendation is evidenced, and its outcome, without changing the state of the action in the owning remediation model.
inputs: Remediation action reference in the owning model
outputs: New observations where the verification generates evidence
preconditions: A recommendation exists and is addressed to a party
The remediation action is referenced rather than duplicated
The verifying party is authorised for this engagement or its follow-up engagement
effects: Verification outcome is available to escalation and programme reporting
No action state in the remediation model is written by this operation
Failed verification may trigger a new engagement or an escalation reference

functions.name: Close engagement
functions.description: Transition the engagement to a closed state once closure criteria are met, fixing open items, retention triggers and the record set that must be preserved.
outputs: Closed engagement state with closure timestamp
Retention trigger timestamp and computed disposition due date
preconditions: Report or certificate has been issued, or a documented termination reason exists
No unresolved appeal is open unless explicitly carried forward
Retention class has been assigned to each record type
effects: Record set becomes read-only except through amendment or appeal outcomes
Retention clock starts and disposition due date is computed
Reopening requires an authorised transition with a recorded reason

functions.name: Export engagement record to a binding target
functions.description: Project the engagement record set onto a declared external exchange binding, applying the versioned crosswalk and emitting the lossiness notes and conformance level actually claimed.
preconditions: A binding profile exists for the target standard and version
Use and distribution restrictions permit the transmission
Sensitivity classification has been evaluated for the recipient
effects: No source record is modified; the export is a projection
Unmapped concepts are reported rather than silently dropped
Conformance is claimed only at the level supported by recorded validation evidence

composition.purpose: Inherit generic activity semantics - occurrence identity, actor participation, temporal bounds and lifecycle - and specialise them for evidence-against-criteria examination. Generic activity machinery is not redefined here.

Resolve each criterion to an external source identifier and version. This model carries the binding, the selection or tailoring decision and any engagement-local interpretation; it never holds requirement text or the catalogue's own version lifecycle.

composition.target: Examined subject model (product, asset, system, process, organisation)
composition.purpose: Identify assessment subjects by their master identifiers so that findings attach to the authoritative record. Subject state, configuration history and lifecycle remain with the owning model.

Resolve auditors, inspectors, responsible parties and intended users, and point to competence evidence. Qualification, training and competence-registry lifecycle stay with the party model; only engagement-scoped appointment and impartiality declarations are held here.

Link a recommendation to the action record that will be planned, executed and closed elsewhere. This model records issuance and verification observations only, never action state, ownership or closure.

composition.target: Risk register and risk treatment model
composition.purpose: Hand over engagement-scoped risk statements for treatment and residual-risk acceptance. Risk scoring policy, treatment decisions and register lifecycle are not owned here.

composition.target: Test, measurement and laboratory result model
composition.purpose: Consume measured values with their stated uncertainty as evidence. Method validation, calibration traceability and uncertainty evaluation remain with the measurement model; only the decision rule application is local.

Carry the reference from an issued certificate or attestation to the certification decision it feeds, and from the examining body to its accreditation scope. Grant, suspension and withdrawal lifecycles are not owned here.

Supply the evidenced determination and stated grounds that an enforcement measure may cite. Deciding, imposing, appealing at law and executing measures such as withdrawal or recall are entirely outside this model.

composition.target: Audit programme and assurance plan model
composition.purpose: Place the engagement within a multi-engagement programme for prioritisation and coverage reporting. Programme risk assessment, resourcing and its own lifecycle are not modelled here.

composition.target: Records management, retention schedule and disposition model
composition.purpose: Resolve retention classes and hand disposition execution to the owning records model or adopting-Dimension policy. This model holds classification, trigger, hold state and tombstone specification only.

Express the engagement as prov:Activity, evidence and reports as prov:Entity, and auditors and bodies as prov:Agent, using wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAttributedTo and actedOnBehalfOf. Alignment only; provenance reasoning semantics are not reproduced.

composition.target: NIST OSCAL assessment-plan and assessment-results models
composition.purpose: Map plan, observation, finding, risk, reviewed-controls, attestation and assessment-log constructs for exchange in control-assessment contexts. Alignment is versioned separately and no conformance is claimed without validation evidence.

composition.target: OASIS SARIF v2.1.0 result interchange format
composition.purpose: Map findings onto result objects with ruleId, level, kind, locations, fingerprints and baselineState for tool-generated inspection results. The mapping is lossy for pass-type results and is annotated as such.

Express the criteria-to-evidence reasoning of a conclusion as claims, argument and evidence when a structured assurance case is required by the recipient. Argumentation semantics remain owned by SACM.
Apply a common attribution, version-identifier and last-modified pattern to every record in the aggregate so that any content change is signalled uniformly, as OSCAL requires of its root elements.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate a named accountable owner for the engagement record set who is organisationally separate from the engagement team, and record that owner in the package manifest alongside the escalation route.

The owner package must declare which authoritative master system issues engagement identifiers, which surrogate scheme is used when none exists, and which value sets govern engagement type, determination, severity and lifecycle state, each pinned to a version.

The owner package must declare every referenced model it depends on - criteria catalogue, examined subject, party, remediation, risk, measurement, certification, enforcement, programme and records management - and must not fork or copy their content into this model.

The owner package must declare the applicable jurisdictions, the governing requirement standard per engagement type, and the retention schedule authority, since none of these are universal and all change the obligations.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-controlled namespace of the form <dimension-namespace>/wm-act-033/<concept>/<local-id> for locally minted identifiers and code values, and never mint identifiers inside an external standard's namespace. External criteria, control, rule and subject identifiers are carried verbatim in their own namespace with the source version attached. Exchange binding profiles are namespaced by target standard and target version so that a target revision does not collide with an existing binding.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-act-033 (WM-ACT-033, nav path NAV.ACT.REV, domain tag ACT.REV) is the authoritative record for this model's status and review state.
Parent registry entry WM-ACT-009 governs the generic activity semantics this model specialises.
Each ALIGN target is registered as an external alignment with its standard identifier, version and the binding profile version, so that alignment drift is visible without editing the model.

canonicalization_rules: Serialise records with deterministic member ordering and Unicode NFC text normalisation before computing any digest, so that a digest is stable across JSON, YAML and document projections.

Normalise all time values to RFC 3339 with whole seconds and an explicit offset, and retain the originally recorded offset as a separate field where local time carries evidential meaning such as a site visit hour.
Normalise identifiers by trimming whitespace and preserving case exactly as issued by the master system; never case-fold an externally issued identifier.
Exclude volatile transport fields such as retrieval timestamps and cache markers from the canonical form used for sealing an issued report.
patch_rules: Observations, evidence items, custody entries and execution-log entries are append-only from the moment they are recorded; a correction is a new entry that references and supersedes the original.

After a report version is issued and sealed, findings and conclusions may not be mutated in place; change requires an erratum, correction, withdrawal or re-issue that names the superseded version and the reason.
Every patch must carry the acting agent, the activity, the modification timestamp and a new record version identifier; a content change without a version and last-modified change is invalid.
Patches to a criteria binding are prohibited after issuance; a criteria change requires a new engagement or a documented re-issue with restated scope.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new optional field, a new code value in an open value set, or a new binding profile is a compatible change.

Changing the meaning of a determination value, altering a severity grading scheme, changing a decision rule, or narrowing the recurrence-key inputs is breaking and requires a new value-set or scheme version and a migration note.
Exchange binding profiles are versioned independently of the model, so that adopting a new target-standard revision does not force a model revision.
Consumers must reject a record whose declared value-set or scheme version they do not recognise rather than coercing it to a known value.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the engagement or artifact - for example the audit or inspection management system's engagement number, a regulator's case reference, or an issuing body's certificate number - recorded together with its issuing system and scheme.

Governed global identifier or IRI where one exists, such as a persistent URI minted in the adopting Dimension's governed namespace or an identifier assigned by a recognised registry or accreditation body.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension only when neither of the above exists, recorded explicitly as a surrogate with its minting agent, minting timestamp and the reason no authoritative identifier was available.
A date, report title, file name, sequence label, engagement year or subject name is never an identifier and must not be used as one, alone or in combination.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-times with at least whole seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or the literal Z; a date alone is permitted only where the governing standard defines a date-precision concept such as a period covered or a certificate expiry. Where they differ, event time (when the observed condition, act or non-compliance occurred), activity time (when the examiner performed the procedure, as start and end), observation or collection time (when the observation was captured), and ingestion time (when the record entered the system of record) are stored as separate fields and are never inferred from one another; the originally recorded local offset is retained where the hour of a site visit carries evidential meaning.
